title: Phoenix Protocol: Verify IAM visibility using list-roles (read-only, deterministic).
objectives: Understand the importance of IAM roles in AWS
Learn to list available IAM roles in a AWS account
Identify potential security risks related to IAM roles

mission_brief.situation: You are operating as a secure cloud operator in an authorized sandbox where resources may or may not exist.
mission_brief.mission: Verify access safely using read-only AWS CLI commands without assuming any pre-existing resources.
mission_brief.execution: Run discovery-only commands and validate success by deterministic behavior (successful execution), not resource presence.

content.concept: AWS IAM roles provide a way to grant specific permissions to EC2 instances or other AWS resources. To maintain secure cloud practices, it's essential to monitor and manage IAM roles effectively. Deterministic validation means you confirm the command executed successfully without relyi
content.walkthrough: To verify IAM visibility using list-roles, navigate to the AWS Management Console > IAM dashboard. Select 'Roles' from the sidebar and click on 'List Roles.' This action will display a list of available IAM roles in your AWS account.
checkpoints: Verify that the IAM roles are correctly configured
Check for any unused or unnecessary IAM roles
Identify potential security risks related to IAM role permissions
common_mistakes: Failing to monitor and manage IAM roles regularly
Granting excessive permissions to IAM roles

lab.setup: Ensure AWS CLI is configured with sandbox credentials. Do not create, modify, or delete any resources.
safety: This lab is read-only and will not modify any AWS resources
Make sure you have the necessary permissions to execute this action
Be cautious when listing IAM roles as it may reveal sensitive information

elite_competence.role_simulation: Demonstrate expertise in verifying IAM visibility by executing the list-roles command and identifying potential security risks related to IAM role permissions.

bug_injection.bug: Operator assumes resources must exist and mislabels empty output as failure.
bug_injection.symptom: Student reports 'nothing returned' and believes permissions are broken.
bug_injection.fix: Explain empty-sandbox behavior and validate by successful execution + no errors, not by finding assets.

pass_conditions: The output contains a list of available IAM roles
No errors or exceptions are encountered
fail_conditions: The list-roles command fails due to insufficient permissions
An error occurs while executing the list-roles command

interrogation_questions: What is the purpose of IAM roles in AWS?
How do you configure IAM role permissions effectively?
What are potential security risks related to IAM role permissions?

legal_context.allowed: Executing read-only AWS CLI commands in an authorized sandbox or training account.
legal_context.prohibited: Creating, deleting, or modifying AWS resources without explicit authorization.

resume_bullets: Demonstrated expertise in verifying IAM visibility
Identified potential security risks related to IAM role permissions
